chunks: It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majiluwayh from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Mansur ibn al-Abbas from Sa'id ibn Janah from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
Black dye is beauty for women and a cause of defeat for the enemy.

key_terms.مَكْبَتَةٌ: A cause of defeat / Instilling fear

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on women dyeing their hair black?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to highlight the specific aesthetic and psychological utility of black dye for women, distinguishing it from the more commonly discussed black dye for men. The phrase 'makbatatun lil-'aduw' (a cause of the enemy's defeat or submission) suggests that this adornment serves a strategic purpose, enhancing presence and authority in social or military contexts. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that permissible beautification can carry functional significance beyond mere appearance-wise and spiritually.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 5. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Ali b. Majluwayh from Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from Mansur b. al-Abbas from Sa’eed b. Janah from Sulayman b. Ja’far al-Ja’fari from Abi al-Hassan (a.s.) who said: “
Black dye is the cause of beauty for women and a cause of defeat of enemies.”
